title.en: Volume 47 Biographies 12: Wei Shikang, Liu Ji
title.raw: 卷47 列傳第12 韋世康 柳機 Volume 47 Biographies 12: Wei Shikang, Liu Ji

sentences.zh: 韋世康，京兆杜陵人也，世為關右著姓。

translations.literal: Wei Shikang—Wei Shikang was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; for generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Guanzhong west.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shikang, of Duling in Jingzhao, came from a family that for generations had ranked among the notable surnames of the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 祖旭，魏南幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu was Southern Youzhou Inspector under the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xu had served as inspector of Southern Youzhou under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父夐，隱居不仕，魏、週二代，十征不出，號為逍遙公。

translations.literal: His father Jiong lived in seclusion and did not take office; through the Wei and Zhou dynasties he was summoned ten times and did not emerge, and was styled the Carefree Duke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiong had retired from public life; summoned ten times under both Wei and Zhou, he never accepted appointment and was known as the Duke of Leisure.

sentences.zh: 世康幼而沉敏，有器度。

translations.literal: Shikang in youth was deep and keen, and had breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shikang was thoughtful and quick-witted, with natural capacity and bearing.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At age ten he was summoned by the province as Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten he was recruited by his province as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 在魏，弱冠為直寢，封漢安縣公，尚周文帝女襄樂公主，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Wei, at weak cap he became Direct Attendant, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Pillar of State, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 後仕周，自典祠下大夫曆沔、硤二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served Zhou, rising from Lower Grand Master of Sacrifices through the prefectures of Mian and Qia.
translations.idiomatic: He later served the Zhou, advancing from lower grand master of sacrifices to governor in turn of Mian and Qia.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，授司州總管長史。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Commissioner-General of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, he was made chief administrator on the staff of the Si Province commissioner-general.

sentences.zh: 于時東夏初定，百姓未安，世康綏撫之，士民胥悅。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern regions had just been settled and the people were not yet at peace; Shikang soothed them, and gentry and commoners alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The east had only just been pacified and the populace was still unsettled; Shikang reassured them until officials and people alike were content.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為民部中大夫，進位上開府，轉司會中大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People, advanced to Upper Pillar of State, and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to upper pillar of state, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之作亂也，高祖憂之，謂世康曰：「汾、絳舊是周、齊分界，因此亂階，恐生搖動。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Jiong rebelled, Emperor Gaozu was troubled and said to Shikang: "Fen and Jiang were formerly the boundary between Zhou and Qi; because of this turmoil, I fear unrest may arise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Jiong rose in rebellion, Emperor Gaozu was deeply concerned and told Shikang, "Fen and Jiang were once the border between Zhou and Qi—this uprising may shake the region.

sentences.zh: 今以委公，善為吾守。」

translations.literal: I now entrust this to you—guard it well for me."
translations.idiomatic: I am entrusting it to you now; hold it firmly on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 因授絳州刺史，以雅望鎮之，闔境清肅。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed him Prefect of Jiang, and with his lofty reputation he stabilized the region; the whole jurisdiction was calm and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him prefect of Jiang, where his prestige kept the entire territory tranquil and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 世康性恬素好古，不以得喪幹懷。

translations.literal: Shikang by nature was tranquil and plain, fond of antiquity, and did not let gain or loss disturb his heart.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Shikang was unassuming and drawn to the classics, unmoved by fortune or misfortune.

sentences.zh: 在州嘗慨然有止足之志，與子弟書曰：「吾生因緒餘，夙沾纓弁，驅馳不已，四紀於茲。

translations.literal: While in the province he once sighed with resolve to know when to stop, and wrote to his sons and younger brothers: "My life has rested on leftover threads of fate; long ago I was stained by cap and sash, and have driven on without cease for four decades now.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the province he once declared his wish to know when enough was enough and wrote to his sons and brothers: "I was born into inherited privilege and have worn office and rank without pause for forty years.

sentences.zh: 亟登袞命，頻蒞方嶽，志除三惑，心慎四知，以不貪而為寶，處膏脂而莫潤。

translations.literal: Repeatedly I have received imperial mandates and often governed a region; my aim was to remove the three confusions and my heart was careful of the four knowings—to take not being greedy as treasure, and though amid fat and grease to remain unstained.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly received imperial orders and often held regional posts, striving to clear the three confusions and heed the four knowings—taking integrity as my treasure and remaining uncorrupted amid plenty.

sentences.zh: 如斯之事，頗為時悉。

translations.literal: Matters such as these are quite well known in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct is widely known in our time.

sentences.zh: 今耄雖未及，壯年已謝，霜早梧楸，風先蒲柳。

translations.literal: Though old age has not yet arrived, my prime years are already gone—frost comes early to the parasol tree and paulownia, and wind strikes the rushes and willows first.
translations.idiomatic: I am not yet truly old, yet my strength has faded—like early frost on the parasol and paulownia, or wind that withers rushes and willows before their time.

sentences.zh: 眼暗更劇，不見細書，足疾彌增，非可趨走。

translations.literal: My eyes grow dimmer still and cannot see fine script; my foot ailment increases and I can no longer hurry on foot.
translations.idiomatic: My sight worsens so I cannot read fine characters; my legs grow weaker so I can no longer hurry about.

sentences.zh: 祿豈須多，防滿則退，年不待暮，有疾便辭。

translations.literal: Salary need not be great—when the cup is full, withdraw; years need not wait for evening—when illness comes, resign.
translations.idiomatic: One need not hoard salary—when the measure is full, step back; one need not wait for old age—when illness comes, retire.

sentences.zh: 況娘春秋已高，溫清宜奉，晨昏有闕，罪在我躬。

translations.literal: Moreover Mother's years are already high; warmth and coolness ought to be tended, and if morning and evening are lacking, the fault is mine alone.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my mother is advanced in years and deserves dutiful care; any failure in daily attendance would be my fault alone.

sentences.zh: 今世穆、世文並從戎役，吾與世沖複嬰遠任，陟岵瞻望，此情彌切，桓山之悲，倍深常戀。

translations.literal: Now Shimu and Shiwen are both on campaign, and I together with Shichong again bear distant appointment; climbing the hill and gazing homeward, this feeling is all the keener, and the grief of Mount Huan is twice the usual longing.
translations.idiomatic: Shimu and Shiwen are both away at war, while Shichong and I again hold distant posts—the longing of one who climbs the hill to look homeward grows keener, and the sorrow of Mount Huan is redoubled.

sentences.zh: 意欲上聞，乞遵養禮，未訪汝等，故遣此及。

translations.literal: I intend to report upward and beg to follow the rites of nurturing; not having consulted you, I send this to reach you.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to petition the throne to observe the rites of filial nurture; before asking your views I send you this letter.

sentences.zh: 興言遠慕，感咽難勝。」

translations.literal: Words stirred by distant longing—sobs choke and cannot be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Speaking from afar I am overcome with longing and can scarcely hold back my tears.

sentences.zh: 諸弟報以事恐難遂，於是乃止。

translations.literal: His younger brothers replied that the matter would probably be hard to accomplish, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers answered that the request would likely fail, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 在任數年，有惠政，奏課連最，擢為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After several years in office he had benevolent administration; his memorial assessments were repeatedly top-ranked, and he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in post his rule was benevolent; his performance reports ranked first year after year, and he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 世康寡嗜欲，不慕貴勢，未嘗以位望矜物。

translations.literal: Shikang had few desires and did not covet noble power; he never used rank and standing to condescend to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang cared little for luxury or power and never looked down on others because of his station.

sentences.zh: 聞人之善，若己有之，亦不顯人過咎，以求名譽。

translations.literal: When he heard of others' excellence it was as if it were his own; he also did not expose people's faults and errors to seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced in others' virtues as though they were his own, and never aired others' faults to win praise.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵上庸郡公，加邑至二千五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in noble rank to Duke of Shangyong, with fief increased to two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Duke of Shangyong, with his fief enlarged to two thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年轉吏部尚書，餘官如故。

translations.literal: That year he transferred to Minister of the Civil Service, his other offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became minister of the civil service while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 四年，丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 未期，起令視事。

translations.literal: Before the term was complete he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period ended he was summoned back to duty.

sentences.zh: 世康固請，乞終私制，上不許。

translations.literal: Shikang firmly petitioned, begging to complete private mourning; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang pleaded repeatedly to finish his mourning; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 世康之在吏部，選用平允，請托不行。

translations.literal: While Shikang was in the Ministry of the Civil Service, selection and appointment were fair and even, and private requests did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of the civil service his appointments were even-handed and favor-seeking failed.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，將事江南，議重方鎮，拜襄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, when preparations were made for the Jiangnan campaign, regional commanders were deemed weighty and he was appointed Prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year seven, as the southern campaign was planned, he was made prefect of Xiang when frontier posts were strengthened.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for a transgression.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授安州總管，尋遷為信州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commissioner-General of An, and soon transferred to Commissioner-General of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made commissioner-general of An, then of Xin.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入朝，複拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he came to court and was again appointed Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he returned to court and was again made minister of the civil service.

sentences.zh: 前後十餘年間，多所進拔，朝廷稱為廉平。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years he advanced many men; the court called him incorrupt and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade he promoted many capable men, and the court praised his integrity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 嘗因休暇，謂子弟曰：「吾聞功遂身退，古人常道。

translations.literal: Once on a day of rest he told his sons and younger brothers: "I have heard that when merit is achieved one withdraws—the ancients' constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Once during a holiday he told his sons and brothers, "I have heard that when one's work is done one steps aside—that is the ancients' constant way.

sentences.zh: 今年將耳順，志在懸車，汝輩以為雲何？」

translations.literal: This year I approach sixty; my will is to hang up my carriage—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: This year I near sixty and wish to retire—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 子福嗣答曰：「大人澡身浴德，名立官成，盈滿之誠，先哲所重。

translations.literal: His son Fusi answered: "Father has bathed body and virtue, name established and office achieved; the sincerity of fullness is what the sages valued.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fusi replied, "You have purified body and character, your name and office are complete, and the sages prized knowing when one is full.

sentences.zh: 欲追蹤二疏，伏奉尊命。」

translations.literal: I wish to follow in the tracks of the two Shu and humbly obey your honored command."
translations.idiomatic: We would gladly follow the example of the two Shu and respectfully obey your wish."

sentences.zh: 後因侍宴，世康再拜陳讓曰：「臣無尺寸之功，位亞台鉉。

translations.literal: Later at a banquet Shikang bowed again and stated his resignation: "Your servant has no merit even the size of a inch, yet rank is next to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Later at court he bowed again and said, "I have achieved no merit whatsoever, yet my rank stands just below the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 今犬馬齒濆，不益明時，恐先朝露，無以塞責。

translations.literal: Now the dog and horse's teeth are worn; I add nothing to the enlightened age, and fear I will meet the morning dew first and have no way to fulfill my charge.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is spent and I can no longer serve this enlightened age; I fear I may die before I can answer for my office.

sentences.zh: 願乞骸骨，退避賢能。」

translations.literal: I beg to offer my bones and withdraw to yield to the able."
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to resign and make way for the worthy."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕夙夜庶幾，求賢若渴，冀與公共治天下，以致太平。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I from dawn to dusk strive, seeking the worthy as if thirsty, hoping to govern the realm together with you to reach great peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "From dawn to dusk I strive and seek talent as though thirsty, hoping to govern the realm with you and bring great peace.

sentences.zh: 今之所請，深乖本望，縱令筋骨衰謝，猶屈公臥治一隅。」

translations.literal: Your present request deeply goes against my original hope; even if sinews and bones decline, I still bend you to govern one corner while lying down."
translations.idiomatic: Your request goes against my deepest hope; even if your strength fails, I still need you to govern a region from your couch."

sentences.zh: 於是出拜荊州總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out and was appointed Commissioner-General of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out as commissioner-general of Jing.

sentences.zh: 時天下唯置四大總管，並、揚、益三州，並親王臨統，唯荊州委于世康，時論以為美。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had only four great commissioner-generals—Bing, Yang, and Yi were all personally ruled by imperial princes; only Jing was entrusted to Shikang, and opinion of the time regarded it as admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Only four great commissioner-generals existed in the realm; Bing, Yang, and Yi were ruled by imperial princes, while Jing alone was entrusted to Shikang—a distinction widely admired.

sentences.zh: 世康為政簡靜，百姓愛悅，合境無訟。

translations.literal: Shikang's government was simple and quiet; the people loved and rejoiced in him, and the whole territory had no lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang governed with simplicity and calm; the people loved him and lawsuits vanished throughout his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒于州，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in the province, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he died in office at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上聞而痛惜之，贈賻甚厚。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he grieved and cherished his memory, and bestowed funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and granted lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand General, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general with the temple name Wen.

sentences.zh: 世康性孝友，初以諸弟位並隆貴，獨季弟世約宦途不達，共推父時田宅盡以與之，世多其義。

translations.literal: Shikang was filial and friendly by nature; at first because his brothers' positions were all lofty and honored, only his youngest brother Shiyue did not advance on the official path—they together yielded their father's fields and houses entirely to him, and the age praised the righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and devoted by nature, he saw his brothers rise to high rank while his youngest brother Shiyue lagged in office; the brothers therefore gave him all their father's land and houses, and contemporaries praised their fairness.

sentences.zh: 長子福子，官至司隸別駕。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fuzi reached the office of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fuzi rose to vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 次子福嗣，仕至內史舍人，後以罪黜。

translations.literal: His second son Fusi served to Palace Secretariat Attendant and was later dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Fusi became palace secretariat attendant but was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之作亂也，以兵逼東都，福嗣從衛玄戰於城北，軍敗，為玄感所擒，令作文檄，辭甚不遜。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled he pressed the eastern capital with troops; Fusi followed Wei Xuan in battle north of the city, the army was defeated, and he was captured by Xuangan, who ordered him to compose a proclamation—the wording was very insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and besieged the eastern capital, Fusi fought under Wei Xuan north of the city; defeated and captured, he was forced to draft a rebel proclamation in grossly defiant language.

sentences.zh: 尋背玄感還東都，帝銜之不已，車裂于高陽。

translations.literal: Soon he turned against Xuangan and returned to the eastern capital; the emperor bore a grudge without end and had him torn apart by chariots at Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon deserted Xuangan and returned to the capital, but the emperor never forgave him and had him torn apart by chariots at Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 少子福獎，通事舍人，在東都與玄感戰沒。

translations.literal: His youngest son Fujiang was Communications Attendant and died in battle against Xuangan at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Fujiang, a communications attendant, was killed fighting Xuangan at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 弟洸洸字世穆，性剛毅，有器幹，少便弓馬。

translations.literal: Younger brother Guang—Guang styled Shimu—was by nature firm and resolute, with capacity and ability; in youth he was skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guang, styled Shimu, was resolute and capable and skilled with bow and horse from youth.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐直寢上士。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, upon leaving the sackcloth he became Upper Gentleman of the Direct Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he began his career as upper gentleman of the direct attendants.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，累遷開府，賜爵衛國縣公，邑千二百戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns and was promoted in succession to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo with a fief of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly, rose to pillar of state, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo with twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從季父孝寬擊尉迥於相州，以功拜柱國，進封襄陽郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor he followed his younger uncle Xiaokuan in attacking Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of Xiangyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor he followed his uncle Xiaokuan against Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou and, for his merit, was made pillar of state and Duke of Xiangyang with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時突厥寇邊，皇太子屯咸陽，令洸統兵出原州道，與虜相遇，擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks raided the border; the Crown Prince encamped at Xianyang and ordered Guang to command troops on the Yuanzhou route; meeting the barbarians he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the frontier the crown prince camped at Xianyang and sent Guang along the Yuanzhou route; he met the enemy and routed them.

sentences.zh: 尋拜江陵總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner-General of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner-general of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以母疾征還。

translations.literal: Before long, because of his mother's illness he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 俄拜安州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Commissioner-General of An.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commissioner-general of An.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，領行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he served as campaign commissioner-general.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commissioner-general.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，拜江州總管，率步騎二萬，略定九江。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified he was appointed Commissioner-General of Jiang, leading twenty thousand foot and horse to pacify Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he became commissioner-general of Jiang and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to secure Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 陳豫章太守徐璒據郡持兩端，洸遣開府呂昂、長史馮世基以兵相繼而進。

translations.literal: Chen's Prefect of Yuzhang Xu Yan held the commandery and wavered between two sides; Guang sent Pillar of State Lü Ang and Chief Administrator Feng Shiji with troops advancing in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan, Chen's prefect of Yuzhang, hedged his allegiance; Guang sent Lü Ang and Feng Shiji with successive columns.

sentences.zh: 既至城下，璒偽降，其夜率所部二千人襲擊昂。

translations.literal: When they reached below the walls Yan feigned surrender; that night he led two thousand of his troops in a surprise attack on Ang.
translations.idiomatic: At the city walls Xu Yan pretended to submit, then that night led two thousand men in a night assault on Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂與世基合擊，大破之，擒璒於陣。

translations.literal: Ang and Shiji joined forces and struck, routing them greatly and capturing Yan in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and Shiji counterattacked, routed the enemy, and captured Xu Yan on the field.

sentences.zh: 高梁女子洗氏率眾迎洸，遂進圖嶺南。

translations.literal: Lady Xi of Gaoliang led her followers to welcome Guang, and he then advanced to take the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi of Gaoliang brought her forces to welcome him, and he pressed on into Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上遣洸書曰：「公鴻勳大業，名高望重，率將戎旅，撫慰彼方，風行電掃，咸應稽服。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Guang a letter: "You, sir, with great merit and great enterprise, high name and heavy standing, lead the army on campaign and comfort that region—like wind and lightning all should submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to Guang: "Your great achievements and high standing lead the army to pacify that region; like wind and lightning all should bow.

sentences.zh: 若使干戈不用，兆庶獲安，方副朕懷，是公之力。」

translations.literal: If arms need not be used and the myriad people gain peace, that will match my heart—it will be your strength."
translations.idiomatic: If war can be avoided and the people live in peace, you will fulfill my dearest wish.

sentences.zh: 至廣州，說陳渝州都督王猛下之，嶺表皆定。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangzhou he persuaded Chen's Commissioner of Yu Region Wang Meng to submit, and the lands beyond the ranges were all settled.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou he persuaded Wang Meng, Chen's commissioner of Yu, to surrender, and the entire south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大悅，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly pleased and permitted him to act at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and authorized him to act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 洸所綏集二十四州，拜廣州總管。

translations.literal: The twenty-four prefectures that Guang soothed and gathered were under him as Commissioner-General of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-four prefectures he pacified were placed under him as commissioner-general of Guang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，番禺夷王仲宣聚眾為亂，以兵圍洸，洸勒兵拒之，中流矢而卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Yi chieftain Wang Zhongxuan of Panyu gathered a crowd in rebellion and with troops besieged Guang; Guang marshaled troops to resist and was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Panyu chieftain Wang Zhongxuan rebelled and besieged him; Guang resisted but was killed by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 贈上柱國，賜綿絹萬段，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Upper Pillar of State, granted ten thousand bolts of silk, with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made upper pillar of state, granted ten thousand bolts of silk, with the temple name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子協嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 協字欽仁，好學，有雅量。

translations.literal: Xie styled Qinren, loved learning, and had refined breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, styled Qinren, loved learning and possessed refined composure.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，後轉秘書郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and later transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as assistant in the bureau of composition and later became secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，其父在廣州有功，上令協齎詔書勞問，未至而父卒。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang his father had merit at Guangzhou; the emperor ordered Xie to carry an edict of commendation, but before he arrived his father died.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang his father had distinguished himself at Guangzhou; the emperor sent Xie with a commendatory edict, but he arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 上以其父身死王事，拜協柱國。

translations.literal: Because his father died in the king's service, the emperor appointed Xie Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in imperial service, the emperor made Xie pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 後曆定、息、秦三州刺史，皆有能名，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Prefect of Ding, Xi, and Qin—all had reputation for ability—and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Ding, Xi, and Qin in turn, earning a name for competence, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 洸弟藝藝字世文，少受業國子。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Yi—Yi styled Shiwen—in youth received instruction at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Yi, styled Shiwen, studied in his youth at the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，數以軍功致位上儀同，賜爵修武縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he repeatedly through military merit reached Upper Pillar of State, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he rose repeatedly through military merit to upper pillar of state and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 授左旅下大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Left Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed lower grand master of the left brigade.

sentences.zh: 出為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，尉迥險圖不軌，朝廷微知之，遣藝季父孝寬馳往代迥。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong secretly plotted rebellion; the court slightly knew it and sent Yi's younger uncle Xiaokuan to gallop and replace Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, Yuwen Jiong plotted treason; the court had wind of it and sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬將至鄴，因詐病，止傳舍，從迥求藥，以察其變。

translations.literal: When Xiaokuan was about to reach Ye he feigned illness, stopped at the relay station, and asked Jiong for medicine to observe his changes.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaokuan neared Ye he feigned illness at a relay station and asked Jiong for medicine to probe his intentions.

sentences.zh: 迥遣藝迎孝寬。

translations.literal: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 孝寬問迥所為，藝党於迥，不以實答。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was doing; Yi sided with Jiong and did not answer truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was up to; Yi, loyal to Jiong, lied.

sentences.zh: 孝寬怒，將斬之，藝懼，乃言迥反狀。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was angry and was about to behead him; Yi feared and then spoke of Jiong's rebellious condition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan grew angry and was about to execute him; terrified, Yi revealed Jiong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 孝寬於是將藝西遁，每至亭驛，輒盡驅傳馬而去。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan thereupon took Yi and fled west; at every post station he would drive off all relay horses and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan then fled west with Yi, at every post driving off all relay horses.

sentences.zh: 複謂驛司曰：「蜀公將至，宜速具酒食。」

translations.literal: He again told the post official: "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive—you should quickly prepare food and drink."
translations.idiomatic: He also told each station master, "The Duke of Shu is coming—prepare food and drink at once.

sentences.zh: 迥尋遣騎追孝寬，追人至驛，輒逢盛饌，又無馬，遂遲留不進，孝寬與藝由是得免。

translations.literal: Jiong soon sent horsemen to pursue Xiaokuan; when the pursuers reached the post they always met lavish feasts and again had no horses, so they delayed and did not advance—Xiaokuan and Yi thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent pursuers; at every station they found feasts but no horses and fell behind, so Xiaokuan and Yi escaped.

sentences.zh: 高祖以孝寬故，弗問藝之罪，加授上開府，即從孝寬擊迥。

translations.literal: Gaozu because of Xiaokuan did not inquire into Yi's crime, added appointment as Upper Pillar of State, and immediately followed Xiaokuan in attacking Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for Xiaokuan, Gaozu did not punish Yi, promoted him to upper pillar of state, and sent him with Xiaokuan against Jiong.

sentences.zh: 及破尉惇，平相州，皆有力焉。

translations.literal: When they broke Yuwen Dun and pacified Xiangzhou, he had strength in both.
translations.idiomatic: He played a major part in defeating Yuwen Dun and pacifying Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，改封武威縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he advanced to Upper Grand General, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Wuwei with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to upper grand general and made Duke of Wuwei with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以修武縣侯別封一子。

translations.literal: As Marquis of Xiuwu he enfeoffed one son separately.
translations.idiomatic: One son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進封魏興郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was advanced to Duke of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was raised to Duke of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜齊州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，士庶懷惠。

translations.literal: His government was clear and simple; gentry and commoners cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was clear and simple, and officials and people alike were grateful.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，遷營州總管。

translations.literal: After several years in office he was transferred to Commissioner-General of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to commissioner-general of Ying.

sentences.zh: 藝容貌瑰偉，每夷狄參謁，必整儀衛，盛服以見之，獨坐滿一榻。

translations.literal: Yi's appearance was grand and imposing; whenever barbarians of the Yi came to audience he would always array guards of honor and wear splendid dress to receive them, sitting alone and filling a whole couch.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was striking in appearance; whenever frontier peoples came to audience he arrayed full guard of honor and splendid dress, sitting alone across an entire couch.

sentences.zh: 番人畏懼，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: The barbarians feared and did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen were awed and dared not meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 而大治產業，與北夷貿易，家資巨萬，頗為清論所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he greatly developed estates and traded with the northern Yi; family wealth reached tens of millions, and he was rather ridiculed in pure discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he amassed great estates and traded with northern tribes until his household wealth reached millions, drawing criticism from moralists.

sentences.zh: 開皇十五年卒官，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang he died in office, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year fifteen he died in office at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懷。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Huai.

sentences.zh: 藝弟沖沖字世沖，少以名家子，在周釋褐衛公府禮曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Chong—Chong styled Shichong—in youth as a son of a famous house, upon leaving the sackcloth under Zhou became Army Ritual Officer of the Duke of Wei's household.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Chong, styled Shichong, entered office under the Zhou as ritual officer in the household of the Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後從大將軍元定渡江伐陳，為陳人所虜，周武帝以幣贖而還之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Grand General Yuan Ding in crossing the river to attack Chen and was captured by the Chen; Emperor Wu of Zhou redeemed him with treasure and returned him.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Yuan Ding across the Yangzi against Chen, was captured, and was ransomed back by Zhou Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝複令沖以馬千匹使于陳，以贖開府賀拔華等五十人及元定之柩而還。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Chong to go to Chen with a thousand horses as envoy, to redeem fifty men including Pillar of State Heba Hua and Yuan Ding's coffin and return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him to Chen with a thousand horses to ransom fifty captives including Heba Hua and recover Yuan Ding's coffin.

sentences.zh: 沖有辭辯，奉使稱旨，累遷少禦伯下大夫，加上儀同。

translations.literal: Chong had eloquence in debate; as envoy he answered the purpose and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Imperial Bearer Grand Master, with Upper Pillar of State added.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent as an envoy, he rose to lower imperial bearer grand master with the added rank of upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 于時稽胡屢為寇亂，沖自請安集之，因拜汾州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiéhu repeatedly made raids and disturbances; Chong himself requested to pacify them and was appointed Prefect of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiéhu raided repeatedly he volunteered to pacify them and was made prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，征為兼散騎常侍，進位開府，賜爵安固縣侯。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned as Concurrent Regular Attendant, advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was summoned as concurrent regular attendant, made pillar of state, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，發南汾州胡千餘人北築長城，在途皆亡。

translations.literal: After more than a year, over a thousand men of the southern Fenzhou Hu were sent north to build the Long Wall, and on the road all fled.
translations.idiomatic: A year later more than a thousand southern Fenzhou Hu sent north to build the Great Wall deserted on the march.

sentences.zh: 上呼沖問計，沖曰：「夷狄之性，易為反覆，皆由牧宰不稱之所致也。

translations.literal: The emperor called Chong to ask his plan; Chong said: "The nature of the Yi and Di is easy to turn back and forth—all is caused by pastoral officials not fitting their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his counsel; Chong said, "Barbarians are quick to turn treacherous when their overseers are unfit.

sentences.zh: 臣請以理綏靜，可不勞兵而定。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests to soothe them with reason; without troubling the army it can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: I can pacify them by just governance without troops.

sentences.zh: 上然之，因命沖綏懷叛者。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and ordered Chong to soothe and cherish the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Chong to win over the deserters.

sentences.zh: 月餘皆至，並赴長城，上下書勞勉之。

translations.literal: Within a month all arrived and all went to the Long Wall; edicts from above and below praised and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month all returned and went to the wall; the court praised them in edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋拜石州刺史，甚得諸胡歡心。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Shi and greatly won the hearts of the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Shi and won the frontier peoples' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 俄而起為南寧州總管，持節撫慰。

translations.literal: Shortly he was recalled as Commissioner-General of Nanning, holding credentials to comfort and soothe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as commissioner-general of Nanning with credentials to pacify the south.

sentences.zh: 複遣柱國王長述以兵繼進。

translations.literal: Again Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops to follow in support.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Wang Changshu was sent with troops in support.

sentences.zh: 沖上表固讓。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Chong petitioned firmly to decline.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「西南夷裔，屢有生梗，每相殘賊，朕甚湣之，已命戎徒，清撫邊服。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Yi tribes of the southwest repeatedly show obstinacy; they constantly slaughter one another, and We greatly pity them. We have already ordered warriors to clear and soothe the border regions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Southwestern tribes repeatedly rebel and slaughter one another; We pity them and have sent troops to pacify the frontier.

sentences.zh: 以開府器幹堪濟，識略英遠，軍旅事重，故以相任。

translations.literal: Because as Pillar of State your capacity and ability can cross difficulties, your insight and strategy are heroic and far-reaching, and military affairs are weighty, We therefore entrust you.
translations.idiomatic: Your capacity and insight suit military command, and We therefore entrust this mission to you.

sentences.zh: 知在艱疚，日月未多，金革奪情，蓋有通式。

translations.literal: Knowing you are in the hardship of mourning and the days and months are not many, the metal and leather seizing feeling—there is a general rule.
translations.idiomatic: Though your mourning is recent, custom allows service to resume in wartime.

sentences.zh: 宜自抑割，即膺往旨。」

translations.literal: You should yourself restrain and cut short, and immediately receive the former decree."
translations.idiomatic: Restrain your grief and obey this order at once.

sentences.zh: 沖既至南寧，渠帥爨震及西爨首領皆詣府參謁。

translations.literal: When Chong reached Nanning, chieftain Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to the headquarters to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanning the chieftains Cuan Zhen and the western Cuan leaders all came to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，下詔褒揚之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 其兄子伯仁，隨沖在府，掠人之妻，士卒縱暴，邊人失望。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Boren followed Chong at the headquarters, seized people's wives, and soldiers indulged in violence—the border people lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Boren, serving on his staff, seized women and soldiers plundered until the frontier lost faith.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大怒，令蜀王秀治其事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was greatly angry and ordered Prince of Shu Xiu to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 益州長史元岩，性方正，案沖無所寬貸，沖竟坐免。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator of Yi Region Yuan Yan by nature was upright and square; investigating Chong he showed no indulgence, and Chong in the end was dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yi region chief administrator Yuan Yan investigated without favor and Chong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其弟太子洗馬世約，譖岩于皇太子。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Crown Prince's Libationer Shiyue slandered Yan to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shiyue, crown prince libationer, slandered Yan to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 上謂太子曰：「古人有沽酒酸而不售者，為噬犬耳。

translations.literal: The emperor told the Crown Prince: "The ancients had one whose wine turned sour and would not sell—because of a biting dog.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the crown prince, "The ancients had a wine seller whose stock turned sour because of a biting dog.

sentences.zh: 今何用世約乎？

translations.literal: Now what use is Shiyue?
translations.idiomatic: What use is Shiyue to you now?

sentences.zh: 適累汝也。」

translations.literal: He will only burden you."
translations.idiomatic: He will only burden you.

sentences.zh: 世約遂除名。

translations.literal: Shiyue was thereupon removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 後數載，令沖檢校括州事。

translations.literal: Several years later Chong was ordered to inspect and manage Kuozhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Chong was ordered to inspect Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時東陽賊帥陶子定、吳州賊帥羅慧方並聚眾為亂，攻圍婺州永康、烏程諸縣，沖率兵擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chieftain Tao Ziding of Dongyang and the bandit chieftain Luo Huifang of Wu Region both gathered crowds in rebellion, attacking and besieging Yongkang of Wuzhou and Wucheng and other counties; Chong led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Tao Ziding and Luo Huifang besieged Wuzhou counties; Chong routed them.

sentences.zh: 改封義豐縣候，檢校泉州事。

translations.literal: He changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Yifeng and was made inspector of Quanzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yifeng and made inspector of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋拜營州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner-General of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner-general of Ying again.

sentences.zh: 沖容貌都雅，寬厚得眾心。

translations.literal: Chong's appearance was refined and elegant; generous and thick, he won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Refined in bearing and generous in manner, he won popular loyalty.

sentences.zh: 懷撫靺鞨、契丹，皆能致其死力。

translations.literal: Comforting and soothing the Mohe and Khitan, he could all bring them to devote their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed the Mohe and Khitan until they would fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 奚、霫畏懼，朝貢相續。

translations.literal: The Xi and Xie feared and were in awe; tribute and missions followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi and Xie tribes submitted and sent tribute in succession.

sentences.zh: 高麗嘗入寇，沖率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo once entered in raid; Chong led troops and struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo raided he drove them back by force.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為豫章王暕納沖女為妃，征拜民部尚書。

translations.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Yuzhang Yang Guang took Chong's daughter as consort and summoned him as Minister of the People.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou, Gaozu betrothed Chong's daughter to Prince Yang Guang and made him minister of the people.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 少子挺，最知名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Ting was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Ting was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 從父弟壽壽字世齡。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Shou—Shou styled Shiling.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Shou, styled Shiling.

sentences.zh: 父孝寬，周上柱國、鄖國公。

translations.literal: Father Xiaokuan was Zhou Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaokuan was Zhou upper pillar of state and Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 壽在周，以貴公子，早有令譽，為右侍上士，遷千牛備身。

translations.literal: Shou in Zhou, as a son of an honored house, early had fine reputation, was Right Attendant Upper Gentleman, and transferred to Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou the young noble Shou won early renown as right attendant upper gentleman and thousand-ox guard.

sentences.zh: 趙王為雍州牧，引為主簿。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao was Prefect of Yong Region he drew him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao became prefect of Yong he made Shou his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 尋遷少禦伯。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to Lower Imperial Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to lower imperial bearer.

sentences.zh: 武帝親征高氏，拜京兆尹，委以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally campaigned against the Gao clan he appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and entrusted him with rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned against the Gao he made Shou metropolitan governor of Jingzhao with charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 以父軍功，賜爵永安縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Because of his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，以其父平尉迥，拜夀儀同三司，進封滑國公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, because his father pacified Yuwen Jiong he appointed Shou Pillar of State, Third Rank, advanced to Duke of Hua with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor he made Shou pillar of state, third rank, then Duke of Hua with five thousand households for pacifying Jiong.

sentences.zh: 俄以父喪去職。

translations.literal: Shortly he left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 高祖愛禪，起令視事，尋遷恆、毛二州刺史，頗有治名。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the love of abdication he recalled him and ordered him to resume duties; soon he transferred to Prefect of Heng and Mao—in both he had reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Sui he was recalled to duty, then governed Heng and Mao with distinction.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，以疾征還，卒于家，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang, because of illness he was summoned back and died at home, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year ten he was recalled ill and died at home at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Ding.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，高祖為晉王昭納其女為妃。

translations.literal: In Renshou, Gaozu for Prince of Jin Yang Zhao took his daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou Gaozu betrothed his daughter to Prince Yang Zhao of Jin.

sentences.zh: 以其子保巒嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baoluan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoluan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 壽弟霽，位至太常少卿，安邑縣伯。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother Ji reached Grand Master of Imperial Sacrifices, Lesser, and Marquis of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Ji rose to vice minister of imperial sacrifices and Marquis of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 津，位至內史侍郎，判民部尚書事。

translations.literal: Jin reached Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently judged Ministry of the People affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin became vice director of the secretariat and concurrently judged civil service affairs.

sentences.zh: 世康從父弟操，字元節，剛簡有風概。

translations.literal: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was firm and simple with spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang's paternal cousin Cao, styled Yuanjie, was stern, principled, and imposing.

sentences.zh: 仕周，致位上開府、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached Upper Pillar of State and Prefect of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to upper pillar of state and prefect of Guang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，以平尉迥功，進位柱國，封平桑郡公，曆青、荊二州總管，卒官。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, for merit in pacifying Yuwen Jiong he advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingsang, and served in succession as Commissioner-General of Qing and Jing—he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor he was made pillar of state and Duke of Pingsang for pacifying Jiong, then commissioner-general of Qing and Jing until he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靜。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 柳機，字匡時，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ji—Ji styled Kuangshi—was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, styled Kuangshi, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父慶，魏尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Father Qing was Wei Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing was left vice director of the secretariat under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 機偉儀容，有器局，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: Ji had grand bearing and capacity, and was quite versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had imposing presence and breadth of vision and was well read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年十九，周武帝時為魯公，引為記室。

translations.literal: At age nineteen, in the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou when he was Duke of Lu, he was drawn as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, when Zhou Emperor Wu was still Duke of Lu, Ji became his recorder.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，自宣納上士累遷少納言、太子宮尹，封平齊縣公。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, from Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat he was promoted in succession to Lower Chamberlain and Palace Chamberlain of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor succeeded he rose from secretariat gentleman to lower chamberlain and palace chamberlain of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi.

sentences.zh: 從帝平齊，拜開府，轉司宗中大夫。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi he was appointed Pillar of State and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was made pillar of state, then grand master of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，遷禦正上大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he transferred to Upper Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he became upper grand master of imperial rectification.

sentences.zh: 機見帝失德，屢諫不聽，恐禍及己，托于鄭譯，陰求出外，於是拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji saw the emperor's loss of virtue and repeatedly remonstrated without being heeded; fearing disaster would reach himself, he entrusted himself to Zheng Yi and secretly sought to go outside, and was thereupon appointed Prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's debauchery and failing to reform him, Ji feared for his life, relied on Zheng Yi, and secured appointment as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作相，征還京師。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時周代舊臣皆勸禪讓，機獨義形於色，無所陳請。

translations.literal: At that time the old ministers of the Zhou all urged abdication; Ji alone showed righteousness in his countenance and made no memorial request.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou ministers urged abdication Ji alone showed open disapproval and made no petition.

sentences.zh: 俄拜衛州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，進爵建安郡公，邑二千四百戶，征為納言。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne he advanced in noble rank to Duke of Jian'an with a fief of twenty-four hundred households and was summoned as Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Sui he was raised to Duke of Jian'an with twenty-four hundred households and made chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 機性寬簡，有雅望，然當近侍，無所損益，又好飲酒，不親細務，在職數年，複出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji by nature was generous and simple, with refined standing, yet while serving in close attendance he made no additions or subtractions; he also loved drinking wine and did not attend to fine affairs—in office several years he again went out as Prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Though refined and respected, he drank heavily, neglected detail, and after years at court returned to Hua as prefect.

sentences.zh: 奉詔每月朝見。

translations.literal: He received an edict to attend court monthly.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to attend court monthly.

sentences.zh: 尋轉冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to Prefect of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 後征入朝，以其子述尚蘭陵公主，禮遇益隆。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to court; because his son Shu married Princess Lanling, favor and treatment grew richer.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he gained favor when his son Shu married Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 初，機在周，與族人文城公昂俱曆顯要。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji was in Zhou, he together with his clansman the Duke of Wencheng Ang both held prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou days he and his kinsman Duke Ang of Wencheng had both held high office.

sentences.zh: 及此，機、昂並為外職，楊素時為納言，方用事，因上賜宴，素戲機曰：「二柳俱摧，孤楊獨聳。」

translations.literal: By this time Ji and Ang were both in outer posts; Yang Su at the time was Chamberlain and just then wielded power—therefore at an imperial feast Su jested to Ji: "Both willows are broken down; the lone poplar stands tall alone."
translations.idiomatic: Now Ji and Ang served in the provinces while Yang Su, chamberlain and favorite, jested at court: "Both willows are broken; the lone poplar stands tall.

sentences.zh: 坐者歡笑，機竟無言。

translations.literal: Those seated laughed; Ji in the end had no words.
translations.idiomatic: The company laughed; Ji said nothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還州。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his province.

sentences.zh: 前後作牧，俱稱寬惠。

translations.literal: Before and after as governor he was all called generous and kind.
translations.idiomatic: As regional governor he was always praised for lenient rule.

sentences.zh: 後數年，以疾征還京師，卒于家，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Several years later, because of illness he was summoned back to the capital and died at home, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, recalled ill, he died at home at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、青州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand General and Prefect of Qing, with posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general and prefect of Qing with the temple name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子述嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子述柳述，字業隆，性明敏，有幹略，頗涉文藝。

translations.literal: Shu—Liu Shu styled Yelong—was by nature bright and keen, had capacity and strategy, and was quite versed in literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Yelong, was clever, capable, and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 少以父廕，為太子親衛。

translations.literal: In youth through his father's shade he became Close Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he became a close guard of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 後以尚主之故，拜開府儀同三司、內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Later because of marrying the princess he was appointed Pillar of State with the insignia of office, Third Rank, and Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage to an imperial princess brought him pillar of state with insignia of office and vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上于諸婿中，特所寵敬。

translations.literal: Among all the sons-in-law the emperor especially favored and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the imperial sons-in-law the emperor favored and respected him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，判兵部尚書事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he concurrently judged Ministry of War affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱去職。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起攝給事黃門侍郎事，襲爵建安郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to act as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Vice Director, inheriting the noble rank Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as acting vice director of the yellow gate and inherited the dukedom of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，判吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: In Renshou he concurrently judged Ministry of the Civil Service affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he was given concurrent charge of the civil service ministry.

sentences.zh: 述雖職務修理，為當時所稱，然不達大體，暴於馭下，又怙寵驕豪，無所降屈。

translations.literal: Though Shu's duties were well ordered and praised in the age, he did not comprehend the larger pattern, was harsh in controlling subordinates, and also relied on favor and was arrogant and overbearing, bowing to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Though efficient and praised at court, he lacked breadth of vision, bullied subordinates, and grew arrogant on imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 楊素時稱貴幸，朝臣莫不讋憚，述每陵侮之，數於上前面折素短。

translations.literal: Yang Su at the time was called honored and favored; court ministers all feared him—Shu each time insulted him and several times before the emperor exposed Su's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su then dominated the court, yet Shu repeatedly humiliated him and exposed his faults before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 判事有不合素意，素或令述改之，輒謂將命者曰：「語僕射，道尚書不肯。」

translations.literal: When judging affairs did not accord with Su's intent, Su sometimes ordered Shu to change them; he would tell the bearer of orders: "Tell the Vice Director—the Minister says he will not."
translations.idiomatic: When Su ordered him to alter a decision Shu refused, telling the messenger, "Tell the Vice Director the Minister will not.

sentences.zh: 素由是銜之。

translations.literal: Su thereby bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Su therefore nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 俄而楊素亦被疏忌，不知省務。

translations.literal: Shortly Yang Su was also distanced and suspected, not knowing provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Su too fell from favor and neglected his duties.

sentences.zh: 述任寄逾重，拜兵部尚書，參掌機密。

translations.literal: Shu's commission grew heavier; he was appointed Minister of War and shared in confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's responsibilities grew; he became minister of war and shared state secrets.

sentences.zh: 述自以無功可紀，過叨匪服，抗表陳讓。

translations.literal: Shu himself thought he had no merit to record and had excessively received unfitting rank; he submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had no merit for such rank, he petitioned to resign.

sentences.zh: 上許之，令攝兵部尚書事。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted it and ordered him to act as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had him act as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上于仁壽宮寢疾，述與楊素、黃門侍郎元岩等侍疾宮中。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace, Shu together with Yang Su, Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Yan, and others attended the illness in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Shu attended him with Yang Su and Yuan Yan.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子無禮于陳貴人，上知而大怒，因令述召房陵王。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince was disrespectful to Lady Chen; when the emperor knew he was greatly angry and ordered Shu to summon the Prince of Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the crown prince had insulted Lady Chen, the emperor angrily ordered Shu to summon Prince Yong of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 述與元岩出外作敕書，楊素聞之，與皇太子協謀，便矯詔執述、岩二人，持以屬吏。

translations.literal: Shu and Yuan Yan went outside to draft the edict; Yang Su heard and conspired with the Crown Prince, then forged an edict to arrest Shu and Yan and hand them to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Yuan Yan went out to draft the edict; Yang Su conspired with the crown prince, forged orders, and had them arrested.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，述竟坐除名，與公主離絕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed for the offense and separated from the princess.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Shu was dismissed and separated from the princess.

sentences.zh: 徙述于龍川郡。

translations.literal: Shu was banished to Longchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Longchuan.

sentences.zh: 公主請與述同徙，帝不聽，事見《列女傳》。

translations.literal: The princess requested to be banished with Shu; the emperor did not listen—the matter is recorded in the "Biographies of Exemplary Women" (Lie nü zhuan).
translations.idiomatic: The princess asked to share his exile; the emperor refused—the account appears in the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》.

sentences.zh: 述在龍川數年，複徙寧越，遇瘴癘而死，時年三十九。

translations.literal: After several years in Longchuan he was again banished to Ningyue; encountering miasma he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After years in Longchuan he was moved to Ningyue, where miasma killed him at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 弟旦旦字匡德，工騎射，頗涉書籍。

translations.literal: Younger brother Dan—Dan styled Kuangde—was skilled at mounted archery and quite versed in books.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dan, styled Kuangde, excelled at horsemanship and archery and was well read.

sentences.zh: 起家周左侍上士，累遷兵部下大夫。

translations.literal: He began his career as Zhou Left Attendant Upper Gentleman and was repeatedly promoted to Lower Grand Master of War.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under the Zhou as left attendant upper gentleman and rose to lower grand master of war.

sentences.zh: 頃之，益州總管王謙起逆，拜為行軍長史，從梁睿討平之，以功授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shortly Commissioner-General Wang Qian of Yi rose in rebellion; he was appointed Campaign Chief Administrator and followed Liang Rui in suppressing and pacifying him; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian of Yi rebelled he served as campaign chief administrator under Liang Rui and was made pillar of state, third rank.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，加授開府，封新城縣男，遷授掌設驃騎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was additionally appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Baron of Xincheng, and transferred to command the Setting Pillar of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year one he was made pillar of state, enfeoffed Baron of Xincheng, and given command of the setting pillar of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 曆羅、淅、魯三州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of Luo, Xi, and Lu—all had reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Luo, Xi, and Lu in turn, all with a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 大業初，拜龍川太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Prefect of Longchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Daye he was made prefect of Longchuan.

sentences.zh: 民居山洞，好相攻擊，旦為開設學校，大變其風。

translations.literal: The people lived in mountain caves and loved to attack one another; Dan established schools and greatly changed their customs.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in mountain caves and raided one another until Dan founded schools and transformed their ways.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之，下詔褒美。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he approved and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him in an edict.

sentences.zh: 四年，征為太常少卿，攝判黃門侍郎事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and acted as Concurrent Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was recalled as vice minister of imperial sacrifices and acting vice director of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子燮，官至河內掾。

translations.literal: His son Xie reached the office of Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie rose to administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 旦弟肅肅字匡仁，少聰敏，閑於占對。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Su—Su styled Kuangren—in youth was clever and keen, skilled in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger brother Su, styled Kuangren, was clever and quick in debate from youth.

sentences.zh: 起家周齊王文學。

translations.literal: He began his career as Literary Scholar to Prince Wen of Qi under the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began under the Zhou as literary scholar to Prince Wen of Qi.

sentences.zh: 武帝見而異之，召拜宣納上士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu saw him and was struck by him; he was summoned and appointed Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wu was impressed and appointed him upper gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，引為賓曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Guest Army Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor he was made guest army officer.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Crown Prince Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince libationer.

sentences.zh: 陳使謝泉來聘，以才學見稱，詔肅宴接，時論稱其華辯。

translations.literal: When Chen envoy Xie Quan came on a mission, because of literary talent he was praised; an edict ordered Su to entertain him—opinion of the time called his brilliance and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen envoy Xie Quan came, Su was ordered to entertain him and was praised for eloquence.

sentences.zh: 轉太子內舍人，遷太子僕。

translations.literal: He transferred to Crown Prince Inner Attendant and was promoted Crown Prince Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He became crown prince inner attendant, then crown prince steward.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，坐除名為民。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed he sat for dismissal and was made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 大業中，帝與段達語及庶人罪惡之狀，達雲：「柳肅在宮，大見疏斥。」

translations.literal: In Daye the emperor spoke with Duan Da about the deposed heir's wicked conduct; Da said: "Liu Su in the palace was greatly slighted and rejected."
translations.idiomatic: In Daye the emperor discussed the deposed heir with Duan Da, who said Liu Su had been greatly slighted in the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「學士劉臻，嘗進章仇太翼于宮中，為巫蠱事。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he answered: "Scholar Liu Zhen once introduced Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for witchcraft affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. Duan Da answered, "The scholar Liu Zhen once brought Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 肅知而諫曰：'殿下帝之塚子，位當儲貳，誡在不孝，無患見疑。

translations.literal: Su knew and remonstrated: "Your Highness is the emperor's heir by tomb and shrine; your station should be heir apparent—caution lies in unfilial conduct, not in being suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Su warned, "You are the emperor's heir—beware unfilial conduct, not suspicion."

sentences.zh: 劉臻書生，鼓搖脣舌，適足以相誑誤，願殿下勿納之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen is a bookish man who wags his lips and tongue—he is fit only to deceive and mislead; I beg Your Highness not to accept him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen is a scholar who wags his tongue—do not heed him.

sentences.zh: '庶人不懌，他日謂臻曰：'汝何故漏泄，使柳肅知之，令面折我？

translations.literal: The deposed heir was displeased and another day said to Zhen: "Why did you leak it and let Liu Su know, making him rebuke me to my face?
translations.idiomatic: The deposed heir was displeased and later demanded of Zhen, "Why did you leak this so Liu Su could rebuke me to my face?"

sentences.zh: '自是後言皆不用。」

translations.literal: From then on his words were not heeded."
translations.idiomatic: After that his counsel went unheeded."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「肅橫除名，非其罪也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Su was rashly removed from the rolls—not his crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Su was wrongly dismissed—it was not his fault."

sentences.zh: 召守禮部侍郎，轉工部侍郎，大見親任。

translations.literal: He was summoned to act as Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to Vice Minister of Works, and greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of rites, then works, and greatly trusted.

sentences.zh: 每行幸遼東，常委之于涿郡留守。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he repeatedly entrusted him to remain and guard at Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: On each Liaodong campaign he left Su as guardian at Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 從弟雄亮雄亮字信誠。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Xiongliang—Xiongliang styled Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Xiongliang, styled Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 父檜，仕周華陽太守。

translations.literal: Father Hui served as Zhou Prefect of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was prefect of Huayang under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 遇黃眾寶作亂，攻陷華陽，檜為賊所害。

translations.literal: Encountering Huang Zhongbao's rebellion, Huayang was attacked and taken; Hui was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Zhongbao rebelled and took Huayang, Hui was killed.

sentences.zh: 雄亮時年十四，哀毀過禮，陰有復仇之志。

translations.literal: Xiongliang was then fourteen; his grief and destruction exceeded the rites, and secretly he had the will to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongliang was fourteen; his mourning exceeded propriety and he secretly vowed revenge.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，眾寶率其所部歸於長安，帝待之甚厚。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time Zhongbao led his followers in submission to Chang'an; the emperor treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhongbao submitted to Chang'an and was generously treated by Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 雄亮手斬眾寶於城中，請罪闕下，帝特原之。

translations.literal: Xiongliang with his own hand beheaded Zhongbao in the city and requested punishment below the gate; the emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongliang slew Zhongbao in the city and surrendered for punishment; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋治梁州總管記室，遷湖城令，累遷內史中大夫，賜爵汝陽縣子。

translations.literal: Soon he managed the records office of the Liang Region Commissioner-General, transferred to Magistrate of Hucheng, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Viscount of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder on the Liang commissioner-general's staff, then magistrate of Hucheng, then secretariat grand master and Viscount of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難作亂江北，高祖令雄亮聘于陳，以結鄰好。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled north of the river, Gaozu ordered Xiongliang to go on mission to Chen to secure neighborly good relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan rebelled, Gaozu sent him to Chen to secure an alliance.

sentences.zh: 及還，會高祖受禪，拜尚書考功侍郎，尋遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When he returned, Gaozu had received the abdication; he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat for Merit Evaluation and soon transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Gaozu had taken the throne; he became vice director for merit evaluation, then yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚書省凡有奏事，雄亮多所駁正，深為公卿所憚。

translations.literal: Whenever the Secretariat had memorials to present, Xiongliang many times rejected and corrected them, and the public ministers deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He often rejected Secretariat memorials and was feared by the ministers.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官檢校太子左庶子，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: Shortly with his original office he inspected and acted as Left Heir Apparent of the Crown Prince, advanced in noble rank to Earl.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting left heir apparent of the crown prince and raised to earl.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊之鎮隴右也，出為秦州總管府司馬，領山南道行台左丞，卒官，時年五十一。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qin Jun went to secure Longyou he went out as Chief Administrator of the Qin Region Commissioner-General's office, concurrently Left Assistant of the South Mountain Route Campaign Headquarters—he died in office, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin went to Longyou he served as his chief administrator and south mountain route assistant until he died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 有子贊。

translations.literal: He had a son Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Zan.

sentences.zh: 從子謇之謇之字公正。

translations.literal: Nephew Jianzhi—Jianzhi styled Gongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jianzhi, styled Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 父蔡年，周順州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Cai'nian was Zhou Prefect of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cai'nian was prefect of Shun under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 謇之身長七尺五寸，儀容甚偉，風神爽亮，進止可觀。

translations.literal: Jianzhi's body was seven feet five inches; his bearing was very imposing, his spirit bright and clear, his advance and stop worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi stood seven feet five inches, imposing in bearing and graceful in movement.

sentences.zh: 為童兒時，周齊王憲嘗遇謇之於途，異而與語，大奇之。

translations.literal: As a child, Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou once met Jianzhi on the road, was struck by him and conversed—he greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he met Prince Xian of Qi, who was astonished and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 因奏入國子，以明經擢第，拜宗師中士，尋轉守廟下士。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized entry into the Imperial Academy; through the classics examination he was selected, appointed Master of the Imperial Clan, and soon transferred to Lower Gentleman Guarding the Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the imperial academy, passed the classics examination, and became master of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗有事太廟，謇之讀祝文，音韻清雅，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu once had business at the Grand Temple, Jianzhi read the prayer text with clear and elegant tone and pitch—observers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Reading prayers at the Grand Temple with clear, elegant delivery, he drew every eye.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，擢為宣納上士。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and promoted him to Upper Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and made him upper gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作相，引為田曹參軍，仍諮典簽事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he was drawn as Field Army Officer and still consulted on registry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor he became field army officer and registry adviser.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜通事舍人，尋遷內史舍人，曆兵部、司勳二曹侍郎。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang he was appointed Communications Attendant and soon transferred to Secretariat Attendant, serving in succession as Vice Director of War and Vice Director of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang he was communications attendant, then secretariat attendant, then vice director of war and merit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以謇之有雅望，善談謔，又飲酒至石不亂，由是每梁、陳使至，輒令謇之接對。

translations.literal: The court because Jianzhi had refined standing, was skilled in wit, and also could drink to a stone measure without disorder—therefore whenever Liang or Chen envoys arrived they always ordered Jianzhi to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued his wit and his capacity to drink a stone of wine without disorder, and always sent him to receive Liang and Chen envoys.

sentences.zh: 後遷光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made vice minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 出入十餘年，每參掌敷奏。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving over more than ten years, each time he shared in drafting and presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he helped draft and present memorials.

sentences.zh: 會吐谷渾來降，朝廷以宗女光化公主妻之，以謇之兼散騎常侍，送公主于西域。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun came to submit, the court married the imperial clan daughter Princess Guanghua to them and made Jianzhi Concurrent Regular Attendant to escort the princess to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun submitted, he escorted Princess Guanghua west as concurrent regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 俄而突厥啟民可汗求結和親，複令謇之送義成公主于突厥。

translations.literal: Shortly the Tujue Qimin Qaghan sought marriage alliance; again Jianzhi was ordered to escort Princess Yicheng to the Tujue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk Qimin Qaghan sought alliance he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Türks.

sentences.zh: 謇之前後奉使，得二國所贈馬千餘匹，雜物稱是，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Jianzhi on former and latter missions received over a thousand horses from the two states and miscellaneous goods in proportion—all he distributed to his clan; the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On both missions he received over a thousand horses and gave everything to his kin, leaving nothing at home.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，出為肅州刺史，尋轉息州刺史，俱有惠政。

translations.literal: In Renshou he went out as Prefect of Su and soon transferred to Prefect of Xi—in both he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou he governed Su, then Xi, both with benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Two years later he left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 煬帝踐阼，複拜光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was again made vice minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 大業初，啟民可汗自以內附，遂畜牧於定襄、馬邑間，帝使謇之諭令出塞。
