translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, Qimin Qaghan because he had submitted inward pastured between Dingxiang and Mayi; the emperor sent Jianzhi to instruct him to go beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In early Daye Qimin pastured near the border; the emperor sent Jianzhi to order him beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及還，奏事稱旨，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When he returned his memorial answered the purpose and he was appointed Yellow Gate Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His report pleased the emperor and he was made yellow gate vice director.

sentences.zh: 時元德太子初薨，朝野注望，皆以齊王當立。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuande Crown Prince had just died; court and countryside fixed their hopes—all thought the Prince of Qi would be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yuande died, all expected Prince Qi to succeed.

sentences.zh: 帝方重王府之選，大業三年，車駕還京師，拜為齊王長史。

translations.literal: The emperor was then weighting selections for the princely household; in the third year of Daye when the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three the emperor made him chief administrator to Prince Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝法服臨軒，備儀衛，命齊王立於西朝堂之前，北面。

translations.literal: The emperor in ritual robes faced the hall, fully arrayed guards of honor, and ordered the Prince of Qi to stand before the western court hall, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In full ritual the emperor had Prince Qi stand before the western court hall facing north.

sentences.zh: 遣吏部尚書牛弘、內史令楊約、左衛大將軍宇文述等，從殿廷引謇之詣齊王所，西面立。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of the Civil Service Niu Hong, Secretariat Director Yang Yue, Left Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu, and others from the hall to lead Jianzhi to the Prince of Qi's place, standing facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, Yang Yue, and Yuwen Shu led Jianzhi to stand before the prince facing west.

sentences.zh: 牛弘宣敕謂齊王曰：「我昔階緣恩寵，啟封晉陽，出籓之初，時年十二。

translations.literal: Niu Hong proclaimed the edict to the Prince of Qi: "I formerly through favor of fate was enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went out to the frontier I was twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong proclaimed to Prince Qi, "Through imperial favor I was once enfeoffed at Jinyang; when I first went to my fief I was only twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 先帝立我於西朝堂，乃令高熲、虞慶則、元旻等，從內送王子相于我。

translations.literal: The former emperor established me at the western court hall and ordered Gao Feng, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min, and others from within to send Prince Xiang to me.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor had Gao Feng and others present Prince Xiang to me as companion.

sentences.zh: 于時誡我曰：'以汝幼沖，未更世事，今令子相作輔於汝，事無大小，皆可委之。

translations.literal: At that time he admonished me: "Because you are young and have not yet experienced worldly affairs, I now make Xiang your companion—in affairs great or small you may all entrust them to him.
translations.idiomatic: He warned me, "You are young—in all matters great or small entrust them to Xiang."

sentences.zh: 無得昵近小人，疏遠子相。

translations.literal: Do not draw near petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Do not favor petty men or distance yourself from Xiang.

sentences.zh: 若從我言者，有益於社稷，成立汝名行。

translations.literal: If you follow my words it will benefit the altars of soil and grain and establish your name and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: If you heed this it will benefit the realm and your reputation.

sentences.zh: 如不用此言，唯國及身，敗無日矣。

translations.literal: If you do not use these words, only the state and your person—ruin will be without delay.
translations.idiomatic: If you ignore it, ruin will come swiftly to you and the state.

sentences.zh: '吾受敕之後，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: After I received the edict I held to it in all dealings and did not dare lose it.
translations.idiomatic: I have kept this counsel ever since.

sentences.zh: 微子相之力，吾無今日矣。

translations.literal: Without the strength of Xiang I would have no today.
translations.idiomatic: Without Xiang I would not be emperor today.

sentences.zh: 若與謇之從事，一如子相也。」

translations.literal: If you work with Jianzhi, it is just like Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: Treat Jianzhi as you would Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又敕謇之曰：「今以卿作輔于齊，善思匡救之理，副朕所望。

translations.literal: Again he charged Jianzhi: "Now I make you companion to Qi—think well on the principle of aiding and saving; match what I hope.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Jianzhi, "Serve Qi as Xiang served me—fulfill my hope.

sentences.zh: 若齊王德業修備，富貴自當鐘卿一門。

translations.literal: If the Prince of Qi's virtue and enterprise are cultivated and complete, wealth and honor will naturally be heaped on your whole house.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi cultivates virtue, your whole house will prosper.

sentences.zh: 若有不善，罪亦相及。」

translations.literal: If there is what is not good, guilt will also reach you."
translations.idiomatic: If he errs, you will share the guilt."

sentences.zh: 時齊王正擅寵，左右放縱，喬令則之徒，深見昵狎。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi was just then monopolizing favor; his close attendants were unrestrained—men like Qiao Lingze were deeply drawn near and pampered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi then held favor and his intimates, including Qiao Lingze, ran wild.

sentences.zh: 謇之雖知其罪失，不能匡正。

translations.literal: Jianzhi though he knew their faults and errors could not correct and straighten them.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi knew their faults but could not correct them.

sentences.zh: 及王得罪，謇之竟坐除名。

translations.literal: When the prince was guilty, Jianzhi in the end sat for dismissal from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi fell from favor, Jianzhi was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 帝幸遼東，召謇之檢校燕郡事。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned in Liaodong and summoned Jianzhi to inspect and manage Yan commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign the emperor summoned him to oversee Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 及帝班師，至燕郡，坐供頓不給，配戍嶺南。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned the army and reached Yan commandery, he sat because provisions were not supplied and was assigned to garrison in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he was convicted of failing to supply the army and was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 卒于洭口，時年六十。

translations.literal: He died at Kuangkou, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Kuangkou at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子威明。

translations.literal: His son Weiming.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Weiming.

sentences.zh: 族弟昂昂字千里。

translations.literal: Clansman Ang—Ang styled Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Ang, styled Qianli.

sentences.zh: 父敏，有高名，好禮篤學，治家如官。

translations.literal: Father Min had a lofty reputation, loved rites and pursued learning deeply, and managed the household like an office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min was renowned for propriety, learning, and running his household with official discipline.

sentences.zh: 仕周，曆職清顯。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he held offices of clear prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he held prominent offices.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為太子太保。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang he was Crown Prince Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang he became crown prince grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 昂有器識，幹局過人。

translations.literal: Ang had capacity and insight; his organizing ability surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had vision and administrative talent beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為大內史，賜爵文城郡公，致位開府，當途用事，百僚皆出其下。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time he was Grand Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Duke of Wencheng, reached Pillar of State, held power on the road, and all hundred officials were below him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he was grand secretariat director, Duke of Wencheng, pillar of state, and dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，稍被疏遠，然不離本職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he was gradually distanced, yet did not leave his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was gradually sidelined but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，深自結納。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor he deeply bound himself in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor he allied himself closely with him.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅之，以為大宗伯。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased with him and made him Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and appointed him grand director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 昂受拜之日，遂得偏風，不能視事。

translations.literal: On the day Ang received the appointment he immediately suffered partial wind-stroke and could not handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his appointment he suffered a stroke and could not take up his duties.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，昂疾愈，加上開府，拜潞州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication Ang's illness healed; he was added Upper Pillar of State and appointed Prefect of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne Ang recovered, was made upper pillar of state, and appointed prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 昂見天下無事，可以勸學行禮，因上表曰：

translations.literal: Ang saw that under heaven all was peaceful and one could encourage learning and practice rites; he therefore submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm at peace, Ang memorialized that learning and ritual should be promoted:

sentences.zh: 臣聞帝王受命，建學制禮，故能移既往之風，成惟新之俗。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that emperors and kings receive the Mandate, establish schools and fix rites—thereby they can shift the customs of the past and complete the habits of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that rulers who receive the Mandate establish schools and fix rites to transform old customs and shape new ones.

sentences.zh: 自魏道將謝，分割九區，關右、山東，久為戰國，各逞權詐，俱殉干戈，賦役繁重，刑政嚴急。

translations.literal: From the time the Wei way was about to decline, the realm was divided into nine regions; Guanzhong west and Shandong east long were battle states; each displayed power and deceit and all died for arms—the levies and corvée were heavy and punishments severe.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei declined the land was divided; east and west warred for generations under heavy taxes and harsh law.

sentences.zh: 蓋救焚拯溺，無暇從容，非朝野之願，以至於此。

translations.literal: It was only rescuing from fire and saving from drowning—there was no leisure for ease; it was not the wish of court and countryside that things came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Men had no leisure but to rescue the realm from fire and flood—it was not their wish that culture should perish.

sentences.zh: 晚世因循，遂成希慕，俗化澆敝，流宕忘反，自非天然上哲，挺生於時，則儒雅之道，經禮之制，衣冠民庶，莫肯用心。

translations.literal: In later ages they followed precedent and thus formed rare admiration; customs turned shallow and debased, drifting and forgetting return—unless by nature a sage above, born in the age, then the way of the ru and the system of canonical rites, officials and people, none would apply their minds.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages followed bad precedent until ritual collapsed unless a sage arose.

sentences.zh: 世事所以未清，軌物由茲而壞。

translations.literal: The reason affairs of the age are not yet clear and standards of things are thereby ruined lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the age remained unsettled and standards decayed.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下稟靈上帝，受命昊天，合三陽之期，膺千祀之運。

translations.literal: Your servant bows that Your Majesty received spirit from the Supreme Lord, received the Mandate from vast Heaven, united the period of the three yangs, and bore the fortune of a thousand sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the Mandate of Heaven and the fortune of a thousand reigns.

sentences.zh: 往者周室頹毀，區宇沸騰，聖策風行，神謀電發，端坐廊廟，蕩滌萬方，俯順幽明，君臨四海。

translations.literal: Formerly the Zhou house collapsed and the realm seethed; holy strategies ran like wind and divine plans flashed like lightning—sitting upright in the hall, washing clean the myriad regions, bending to follow dark and bright, ruling the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou fell You swept the realm clean and ruled all within the seas.

sentences.zh: 擇萬古之典，無善不為；

translations.literal: Choosing the canons of ten thousand ages—where there was good, none was not done;
translations.idiomatic: You chose the best of antiquity and did every good thing;

sentences.zh: 改百王之弊，無惡不盡。

translations.literal: reforming the abuses of a hundred kings—where there was evil, none was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: and reformed every abuse of past kings.

sentences.zh: 至若因情緣義，為其節文，故以三百三千，事高前代。

translations.literal: As for following feeling and joining with righteousness to make their regulated text, therefore with three hundred and three thousand matters it towers above former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your ritual code of three hundred and three thousand rules surpasses all former ages.

sentences.zh: 然下土黎獻，尚未盡行。

translations.literal: Yet the people below and the tribute bearers have not yet fully carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the common people have not yet fully adopted it.

sentences.zh: 臣謬蒙獎策，從政籓部，人庶軌儀，實見多闕，儒風以墜，禮教猶微，是知百姓之心，未能頓變。

translations.literal: Your servant wrongly received praise and encouragement, followed government in a frontier department—the people's standards and ceremonies truly show many lacks; ru wind thereby falls and ritual teaching is still slight—thus one knows the hearts of the hundred surnames cannot suddenly change.
translations.idiomatic: In my own province I see how far the people still fall short of ritual.

sentences.zh: 仰惟深思遠慮，情念下民，漸被以儉，使至於道。

translations.literal: Looking up, Your Majesty's deep thought and far consideration cherishes the people below; gradually cover them with frugality so they reach the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to continue to lead the people toward the Way through frugality.

sentences.zh: 臣恐業淹事緩，動延年世。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the enterprise will be submerged and affairs delayed, moving and extending the years.
translations.idiomatic: I fear delay will cost years of progress.

sentences.zh: 若行禮勸學，道教相催，必當靡然向風，不遠而就。

translations.literal: If one practices rites and encourages learning, the Way teaching mutually urging, they will surely turn like wind and arrive without distance.
translations.idiomatic: If rites and learning are urged together, the people will turn like wind and soon arrive.

sentences.zh: 家知禮節，人識義方，比屋可封，輒謂非遠。

translations.literal: Every household will know ritual and regulation, every person will know righteousness and direction—households fit to be enfeoffed; I say it is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Then every household may know ritual and every person know righteousness.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之，因下詔曰：

translations.literal: The emperor read and approved, and issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 建國重道，莫先於學，尊主庇民，莫先於禮。

translations.literal: Establishing the state and weighting the Way—nothing comes before learning; honoring the ruler and sheltering the people—nothing comes before rites.
translations.idiomatic: To establish a state nothing comes before learning; to honor the ruler and shelter the people nothing comes before rites.

sentences.zh: 自魏氏不競，周、齊抗衡，分四海之民，鬥二邦之力，遞為強弱，多歷年所。

translations.literal: From the time the Wei house did not contend, Zhou and Qi opposed each other, dividing the people of the four seas and contending with the strength of two states—alternately strong and weak for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei fell, Zhou and Qi divided the realm and contended for generations.

sentences.zh: 務權詐而薄儒雅，重干戈而輕俎豆，民不見德，唯爭是聞。

translations.literal: They pursued power and deceit and slighted the ru way, valued arms and slighted the sacrificial vessels—the people did not see virtue, only contention was heard.
translations.idiomatic: They prized cunning over learning and arms over ritual until the people knew only contention.

sentences.zh: 朝野以機巧為師，文吏用深刻為法，風澆俗弊，化之然也。

translations.literal: Court and countryside took craft and cleverness as teachers; literary clerks used severity as law—wind poured and customs debased; transformation made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside took craft as teacher and clerks took severity as law until customs were debased.

sentences.zh: 雖複建立庠序，兼啟黌塾，業非時貴，道亦不行。

translations.literal: Though again they established schools and concurrently opened academies, the enterprise was not valued in the age and the Way also was not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Schools were founded but learning was not honored and the Way was not practiced.

sentences.zh: 其間服膺儒術，蓋有之矣，彼眾我寡，未能移俗。

translations.literal: Among them those who wore the ru on their breast—there were some; they were few against many and could not shift customs.
translations.idiomatic: A few still studied the classics but were too few to change the age.

sentences.zh: 然其維持名教，獎飾彝倫，微相弘益，賴斯而已。

translations.literal: Yet in maintaining name and teaching and rewarding and adorning constant norms, slightly mutually expanding benefit—they relied on this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they alone sustained name and teaching and moral norms.

sentences.zh: 王者承天，休咎隨化，有禮則祥瑞必降，無禮則妖孽興起。

translations.literal: Kings inherit Heaven; fortune and calamity follow transformation—if there are rites then auspicious omens surely descend; if there are no rites then portents arise.
translations.idiomatic: Kings inherit Heaven: with rites come omens, without rites come portents.

sentences.zh: 人稟五常，性靈不一，有禮則陰陽合德，無禮則禽獸其心。

translations.literal: People receive the five constants; nature and spirit are not one—if there are rites then yin and yang unite in virtue; if there are no rites then beasts are their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: With rites yin and yang harmonize; without rites men become beasts at heart.

sentences.zh: 治國立身，非禮不可。

translations.literal: To govern the state and establish the person—without rites it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the state and establish the person rites are indispensable.

sentences.zh: 朕受命于天，財成萬物，去華夷之亂，求風化之宜。

translations.literal: We received the Mandate from Heaven, completed the myriad things, removed the disorder of barbarian and Chinese, and sought what was fitting for transformation of customs.
translations.idiomatic: We received Heaven's Mandate, ordered the myriad things, ended barbarian disorder, and sought proper customs.

sentences.zh: 戒奢崇儉，率先百辟，輕徭薄賦，冀以寬弘。

translations.literal: Warning against extravagance and honoring frugality, taking the lead among the hundred ranks; light corvée and thin levies, hoping thereby for broad forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: We warned against extravagance, lightened burdens, and sought broad relief for the people.

sentences.zh: 而積習生常，未能懲革，閭閻士庶，吉凶之禮，動悉乖方，不依制度。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated habits become constant and could not be punished and reformed; in lanes and hamlets, gentry and commoners, rites of fortune and calamity—all moved contrary to the norm, not following the system.
translations.idiomatic: Yet old habits remained; gentry and commoners alike violated ritual norms.

sentences.zh: 執憲之職，似塞耳而無聞，蒞民之官，猶蔽目而不察。

translations.literal: Those holding the law seemed to stop their ears and not hear; officials facing the people were still as if covering their eyes and not inspecting.
translations.idiomatic: Law officers seemed deaf; local officials seemed blind.

sentences.zh: 宣揚朝化，其若是乎？

translations.literal: To proclaim and spread court transformation—is it like this?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how court transformation is proclaimed?

sentences.zh: 古人之學，且耕且養。

translations.literal: Learning of the ancients—both plowing and nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients both plowed and studied.

sentences.zh: 今者民丁非役之日，農畝時候之餘，若敦以學業，勸以經禮，自可家慕大道，人希至德。

translations.literal: Now on days when the people are not on corvée and in the seasons of farming, if we thickly urge them with learning and encourage them with canonical rites, of themselves families will admire the Great Way and people will hope for utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On days free from corvée, if we urge study and ritual, families will turn to the Way.

sentences.zh: 豈止知禮節，識廉恥，父慈子孝，兄恭弟順者乎？

translations.literal: Will it stop at knowing ritual and regulation, recognizing integrity and shame, fathers kind and sons filial, elder brothers respectful and younger brothers obedient?
translations.idiomatic: They will know ritual, shame, and filial piety as well.

sentences.zh: 始自京師，爰及州郡，宜祗朕意，勸學行禮。

translations.literal: Beginning from the capital, extending to prefectures and commanderies—all should respect Our intent and encourage learning and practice rites.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to every commandery, all should encourage learning and rites.

sentences.zh: 自是天下州縣皆置博士習禮焉。

translations.literal: From this throughout the realm's prefectures and counties all established erudites to study rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every prefecture and county established erudites to teach rites.

sentences.zh: 昂在州，甚有惠政，數年，卒官。

translations.literal: Ang in the province had very benevolent government; several years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ang governed Lu with benevolence and died in office after several years.

sentences.zh: 昂子調子調，起家秘書郎，尋轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Ang's son Diao—Diao began his career as Secretariat Gentleman and soon transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's son Diao began as secretariat gentleman and became attending censor.

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊素嘗於朝堂見調，因獨言曰：「柳條通體弱，獨搖不須風。」

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yang Su once saw Diao in the court hall and spoke alone: "The willow branch is weak throughout—only it sways without needing wind."
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Yang Su once said to Diao alone, "The willow is weak all through yet sways without wind.

sentences.zh: 調斂板正色曰：「調信無取者，公不當以為侍御史；

translations.literal: Diao gathered his tablet and with proper color said: "If Diao truly has nothing to take, you should not make him Attending Censor;
translations.idiomatic: Diao replied sternly, "If I am worthless you should not have made me censor;

sentences.zh: 調信有可取，不應發此言。

translations.literal: if Diao truly has what may be taken, you should not have spoken these words.
translations.idiomatic: if I am worthy you should not have spoken thus.

sentences.zh: 公當具瞻之秋，樞機何可輕發！」

translations.literal: You are in the season of being gazed upon by all—how can the pivot lightly speak!"
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the center of power—how can you speak so lightly!

sentences.zh: 素甚奇之。

translations.literal: Su greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Su was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，累遷尚書左司郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was repeatedly promoted to Left Department Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose to left department director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時王綱不振，朝士多贓貨，唯調清素守常，為時所美。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial norm was not strong; court gentlemen mostly took bribes—only Diao was pure and plain, holding constant, and was praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was corrupt only Diao remained pure and was praised.

sentences.zh: 然於幹用，非其所長。

translations.literal: Yet in practical ability it was not his strong point.
translations.idiomatic: Practical administration was not his strength.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：韋氏自居京兆，代有人物。

translations.literal: The historiographer comments: The Wei clan from their residence in Jingzhao for generations had outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Wei of Jingzhao produced outstanding men for generations.

sentences.zh: 世康昆季，餘慶所鐘，或入處禮闈，或出總方嶽，硃輸接軫，成陰，在周暨隋，勳庸並茂，盛矣！

translations.literal: Shikang and his brothers—the surplus of blessed fortune was bell-like; some entered the ritual ministries, some went out to command regions; vermilion wheels met hub to hub, forming shade—in Zhou and Sui merit and service were both lush; magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Shikang and his brothers enjoyed accumulated blessing; some held central posts, some governed regions—a glory spanning Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 建安風韻閒雅，望重當時。

translations.literal: Jian'an's refined elegance and leisurely bearing—heavy in standing at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Ji of Jian'an was refined and widely respected.

sentences.zh: 述恃寵驕人，終致傾敗。

translations.literal: Shu relied on favor and insulted others, in the end bringing overturn and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shu grew arrogant on favor and ended in ruin.

sentences.zh: 旦屢有惠政，肅每存誠讜。

translations.literal: Dan repeatedly had benevolent government; Su always preserved sincere remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Dan governed with benevolence; Su offered sincere remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 雄亮名節自立，忠正見稱，謇之神情開爽，頗為疏放。

translations.literal: Xiongliang established name and integrity by himself and was praised for loyalty and rectitude; Jianzhi's spirit was open and bright and rather free and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongliang was known for integrity; Jianzhi was open and somewhat unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 文城曆仕二朝，鹹見推重，獻書高祖，遂興學校，言能弘道，其利博哉！

translations.literal: Wencheng served two dynasties and in both was pushed and honored; submitting his book to Gaozu, thereby schools were raised—words able to expand the Way; how broad the benefit!
translations.idiomatic: Ang of Wencheng served two dynasties with honor; his memorial to Gaozu raised schools—the benefit of his words was vast indeed!
